resources.string: Distance between neighbouring electrodes. In the Wenner method all four are in line at the same spacing a.
Depth at which the electrodes are driven. Use it when it is not small compared with the spacing.
Distance from the centre of the line to each current electrode (A and B).
Distance from the centre to each potential electrode (M and N). Must be less than AB/2.
Earth tester reading (voltage between M and N divided by the current injected between A and B).
Calculates the apparent soil resistivity from a four-electrode measurement in line. Repeat with larger spacings to see how resistivity changes with depth (vertical electrical sounding).
RIC N°06 (annex 6.6) accepts the Wenner and Schlumberger methods, one per measurement, with wings up to 100 m; 50 m if space is lacking and, exceptionally, 30 m.
Shape of the earth electrode. Each has its formula in table N°6.4 of RIC N°06.
Soil resistivity, ideally measured on site with the resistivity calculator.
Average values from table N°6.3 of RIC N°06, for a first estimate before measuring.
Length of the rod or buried conductor; for a plate, its perimeter.
Estimates the resistance of an earth electrode with the formulas of RIC N°06 (table N°6.4) from its shape and the soil resistivity.
The result is approximate: the standard requires measuring and checking the earthing when it is put into service (clause 9.2).
